subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex - next steps
messages:
From: Anna Bianchi <anna.bianchi@globex.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: pablo.ruiz@globex.com, l10n@globex.com
Date: 2026-06-15T14:08:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — that was very helpful. A few quick follow-ups from our side as we evaluate options: 

- Can you confirm which open models you recommend for conversational customer support in French, German, and Japanese?
- Do you have benchmark links for latency and quality on EU languages vs en-US?
- We can share a sample prompt set from several product flows; what format do you prefer?

We want to make sure we avoid quality regressions when we later roll forward model versions. Also good to have an estimate of cost delta for using a larger model for EU locales vs using the same model across all regions.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Bianchi
Head of Localization & Internationalization
Globex Corporation
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Anna Bianchi <anna.bianchi@globex.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex

Anna — great to connect, and thanks for the clear ask. Recap + proposed next steps below.

Recap from our call:
- Goal: support conversational customer support for EU (fr, de) and APAC (ja) with parity to en-US for intent accuracy and tone.
- Constraints: latency target <250ms p50 token generation for in-session responses; budget target to keep per-utterance cost within 1.5x of current en-US baseline.

Recommended short list (based on initial fit & our internal benchmarks):
- small/medium: Llama3-13B-q4 (quantized) — strong latency, good for short-turn intents, best cost tradeoff.
- large/quality: Redstone-70B (FP16) — best cross-lingual quality, especially for Japanese and formal German.
- fallback/cheap: Mistral-instruct-7B (int8) — good for lower-cost backfills and fallbacks for simple flows.

What I’m attaching: prompt_sets_v1.csv (sample prompts across flows), and our high-level benchmark summary (pdf) with per-language quality metrics and p50/p95 latency on typical Redwood Dedicated instances.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share 200–500 representative prompts/responses (CSV is perfect).
2) We run an eval suite (automatic metrics + spot manual review) across the 3 candidate models for fr/de/ja.
3) Sync within 7 business days with results and a recommended rollout plan (can include canary % and fallback rules).

Do you want us to scope a slightly larger eval set for EU languages (add nl, sv) or stick to fr/de for now?

Thanks — I’ll loop Dev on quantization/latency constraints and Rishi on rollout/fallback policies.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Anna Bianchi <anna.bianchi@globex.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-16T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex

Anna / team — quick technical note on the model options: 

- Llama3-13B-q4 (quantized): expected 40–60% lower token cost vs FP16 on our Dedicated pools with negligible QA delta for short-turn intents. Good latency profile when batching is small (we can prioritize low-latency fast-path).
- Redstone-70B (FP16): best cross-lingual coherence, but p95 latency is higher unless we reserve a slightly larger GPU slice; cost is ~2.2x vs 13B quantized.
- Mistral-instruct-7B (int8): great fallback for non-core flows and for pre-filtering.

Operational suggestions:
- Start with mixed strategy: quantized 13B for most sessions, auto-escalate to 70B for low-confidence or high-complexity prompts (language detection + confidence threshold).
- We can pre-compute a small locale-specific cache for repeated prompts (KB-driven answers) to cut cost and p95 latency.

I’ll queue the eval jobs once we have the CSV. Let me know expected throughput targets so we can provision accordingly.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: pablo.ruiz@globex.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Anna Bianchi <anna.bianchi@globex.com>, l10n@globex.com
Date: 2026-06-17T11:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex

Thanks, Marissa & Dev. Couple clarifications from the localization team: 

- For French and German we need both formal and informal variants evaluated (FR: tu/vous; DE: Sie/du where applicable). Can your evals measure register/tone?
- For Japanese, handling of honorifics and polite/formal forms is critical. Any specific prompts we should include for that?
- Data residency: our security/compliance team will ask whether eval logs for EU customers can be kept in EU-only storage.

We’ll prepare the CSV with columns: locale, scenario, prompt, expected_intent, example_response, sensitivity_flag. Plan to share by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Pablo
Localization Program Manager
Globex
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: pablo.ruiz@globex.com, Anna Bianchi <anna.bianchi@globex.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-18T15:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex

Great questions — answers and next actions below.

Tone/register evaluation:
- Yes, our eval suite includes automated style-scoring (BLEU/COMET variants + a proprietary politeness register classifier) and a small human review panel for edge cases. We will score per-locale and flag examples where the model fails the expected register.

Japanese honorifics prompts:
- Please include representative customer excerpts: customer_name placeholders, polite vs casual responses, and escalation phrases (e.g., apologetic/formal openings). I attached a short example set in prompt_sets_v1.csv.

Data residency:
- We can keep eval logs and manual-review artifacts in EU-only storage for this project when you use our Dedicated or Private offering. I’ve added this as an action item for our Security team; Rishi will follow up with a short checklist.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- You: share CSV with ~300 rows (locale, scenario, prompt, expected_intent, example_response, sensitivity_flag) by 2026-06-22.
- Redwood: run automatic evals within 3 business days of receipt + 10 spot manual reviews; provide per-locale quality matrix and recommended rollout (canary % + fallback rules).
- Decision: agree rollout plan in follow-up call (we can schedule for the week of 2026-06-29).

If that timeline works I’ll create a HubSpot task and trigger the eval queue.

Best,
Marissa
From: Anna Bianchi <anna.bianchi@globex.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: pablo.ruiz@globex.com, l10n@globex.com
Date: 2026-06-20T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals for Globex

Marissa — this all looks good. We’ll share the CSV by 2026-06-22 and we appreciate the EU-only storage option. Two quick asks before we hand off to your security: 

1) Can you include an expected timeline for Rishi to deliver the security checklist (so our InfoSec can schedule a review)?
2) For the manual reviews: can you note whether reviewers have language competency (native or advanced) for fr/de/ja?

Once we have those, I’ll push the CSV over. Looking forward to the results.

Thanks,
Anna
